topic.title: Structured Latent Variables and Disentangled Representations
topic.overview: Latent-variable models explain observations through hidden factors, which may be discrete, continuous, shared, or condition-specific. This topic combines graphical structure with neural encoders and decoders to make those factors useful and interpretable. It studies variational inference, autoencoder regularization, and the assumptions needed to separate different sources of variation.
topic.whyItMatters: A latent coordinate does not become meaningful merely because it reconstructs data well. Independence assumptions, missing observations, and optimization bias can all shape the factors a model discovers. Explicit structure helps express desired relationships, but its interpretation must be checked against the data-generating setting.
topic.evolution: A 2002 multiple-cause vector-quantization model represents independent factors through discrete states. Later work develops denoising and variational autoencoders. In 2023, structured variational methods improve optimization for discrete uncertainty and missing data; DisCoVR in 2026 combines shared and condition-specific representations with adversarial and structured-prior terms to improve separation.
openQuestions: Which aspects of a latent decomposition are identifiable from the available supervision?
How can a shared representation discard condition-specific information while remaining predictive?
